provenance.annotator: Codex authored synthetic gold; independently reviewed before execution
provenance.description: One shared corpus of concise original documents with competing near matches. Gold was authored before execution. This evaluates ingestion, current-version retrieval, scoped search and checked answer behavior; it is not independently sampled population accuracy.
provenance.source_policy: Synthetic corpus metadata is recorded here; originals assert their scoped facts directly. No live-library originals are used.

gold_semantics.required_support: Exact original substrings that must appear in supporting answer references; corrected-premise evidence may appear in refutation references.
gold_semantics.required_dependencies: Exact original substrings that must be retrieved into provider-input windows and bound as verification dependencies when judgment receipts expose them; these may be context bridges rather than supporting citations. For negative or conflicting outcomes with no public matches, the actual provider input still must include these windows.
gold_semantics.forbidden_support: Inapplicable, obsolete, rejected or attack substrings that must not be accepted as supporting or refuting the requested answer. Quotes may occur only in previous_text for version-staleness tests.
gold_semantics.source_exact: For numeric answers, the exact source numeral and normalized source-unit token before conversion (singular English or unchanged Hebrew, matching numeric.unit); values specifies the exact converted decimal string and target unit.
gold_semantics.absence: no_answer_in_evaluated_candidates means the requested fact is not established, never that an unknown fact is false.

long_document_stressor.purpose: Retrieve a decisive end-of-document exception amid overlapping operational paragraphs and combine it with separate membership evidence.

Harbor administrator authentication policy, approved and effective from 2025-01-01 through 2025-12-31: administrators authenticate with an email one-time code. This is the historical rule for those dates; it was superseded on 2026-01-01.

Harbor administrator authentication policy, approved and effective from 2026-01-01 onward: administrators must use a hardware security key. This adopted policy supersedes the 2025 email-code rule and remains the current rule.
Harbor administrator authentication proposal dated 2026-10-20: "Administrators may authenticate with a password alone." The security council rejected this proposal; it was never adopted.
Cedar Europe release authority: Selma is the approver for production releases. Cedar Europe is a separate service from Cedar Americas.
Cedar Americas release authority: Orin is the approver for production releases. This authority applies only to Cedar Americas, not Cedar Europe.
Cedar Europe release coordination: Orin schedules release meetings and maintains the checklist. Scheduling and checklist ownership do not grant release approval authority.

Beacon release policy: a release is eligible to ship only if its approval is signed. A signed approval is necessary but does not by itself establish shipping eligibility; the release board determines the remaining requirements.
Beacon release 42 record: its approval is signed. The release board has not recorded whether release 42 meets the remaining shipping requirements or is eligible to ship.
Beacon release 41 record: its approval is signed and the release board has declared release 41 eligible to ship. This decision concerns release 41 only.

Quarry workspace audit-bundle export policy. Generic guest baseline: guests cannot export audit bundles unless an applicable exception in this policy grants permission. Operational export guidance follows; the final authorization exception is part of this policy.

Request catalog: The audit-bundle export request catalog lists previous request identifiers and processing dates. Listing a request in the catalog is an operational record and does not grant a guest permission to export the bundle.

Preparation queue: An audit-bundle export may be prepared before the requester has download permission. Preparation validates the archive layout only. Guests waiting for preparation remain subject to the export authorization rule.

Packaging: Audit-bundle exports contain audit records and a manifest. The manifest enumerates the stored files and their checksums. A successful packaging check concerns the bundle bytes and does not establish a requester role.

Audit review: The review desk can inspect an audit-bundle export request and record comments. A review comment is not enrollment in the Audit delegation and cannot by itself change a guest export permission.

Notification routing: Export-ready notifications go to the email address on the audit-bundle request. Receiving a notification only establishes that the delivery message was sent; it does not prove that the requester is allowed to export.

Retry handling: If audit-bundle packaging fails, the job may be retried with the original request identifier. A packaging retry does not bypass authorization, change guest membership, or create an additional export permission.

Naming: The filename of an audit-bundle export includes the request identifier and creation date. Similar filenames can refer to different prepared bundles. A filename match is not a membership or authorization record.

Retention: Prepared audit-bundle exports remain available while their source audit records are retained. Availability describes the bundle, not who may download it. Guest authorization is evaluated independently.

Workspace boundary: A Quarry audit-bundle export contains Quarry audit records only. Another workspace cannot grant export permission in Quarry. A guest role or delegation in another workspace does not establish Quarry membership.

Ordinary files: Ordinary project-file exports use a separate access check from audit-bundle exports. The ability to export an audit bundle does not grant a guest permission to export ordinary project notes, attachments or working files.

Temporary links: An audit-bundle export link identifies the prepared archive but is not a bearer permission. Opening the link still requires the applicable authorization check. Sharing the link does not enroll the recipient in any delegation.

Browser download: The browser can display a prepared audit-bundle export after packaging completes. The enabled download control is not the policy itself; the service checks the requester against the audit-bundle authorization rule.

Command-line download: The command-line audit-bundle download operation applies the same authorization rule as the browser. Choosing a different client does not make a guest an administrator or change Audit delegation enrollment.

Audit trail: Every successful audit-bundle export adds an access entry describing the requester and archive. An access entry records a completed event; it is not a standing authorization for later exports by that guest.

Administrative support: An administrator may help locate a guest's audit-bundle export request and inspect its job status. Helping with a request does not automatically transfer the administrator's own permissions to the guest.

Project owners: A project owner can identify which ordinary files belong to the project. Project ownership alone does not enroll anyone in the Audit delegation and does not establish guest authorization for an audit-bundle export.

Cancellation: A requester may cancel an audit-bundle preparation job that they submitted. Permission to cancel a job controls the preparation workflow only; it does not establish permission to download the prepared audit bundle.

Transport errors: A failed connection during audit-bundle transfer can be retried using the same prepared archive. The retry must use the same authorized identity. A connection error is not a change in the guest export policy.

Manifest verification: The audit-bundle manifest can be checked against the downloaded archive. Checksum agreement establishes byte integrity only. It neither proves active Audit delegation enrollment nor authorizes an otherwise blocked requester.

Search results: A search result may list an audit-bundle preparation record without granting access to the bundle. Search relevance, matching text and the visibility of a request title do not establish a guest's export authorization.

Support tickets: A support ticket can mention a guest and an audit-bundle export. Ticket ownership and escalation priority do not change the authorization rule. An operator must consult the active delegation register for membership.

Revocation: When an active delegation enrollment is revoked, the old enrollment record remains as history. Historical membership does not establish current permission. Authorization uses the enrollment status that applies now.

Policy precedence: These operational sections describe preparation and transfer, not a new authorization grant. The applicable authorization exception at the end of this policy controls over the generic guest baseline where its conditions hold.

Identity verification: The audit-bundle export service binds each request to the authenticated Quarry member identity. A shared display name, forwarded link or similar account name is insufficient to establish that member's delegation enrollment.

Final authorization exception, currently approved: guests enrolled in the Audit delegation may export the audit bundle. This exception overrides the generic guest baseline for the audit bundle only. The exception grants no permission to export ordinary project files.
Quarry Audit delegation register: Alba is an enrolled guest member of the Audit delegation. This enrollment is active now.
Quarry ordinary-project access record: Alba is a guest and cannot export ordinary project files. The record does not remove Audit delegation privileges.

Redwood document replacement procedure: call upload with the existing document_id, the current expected_version, and replacement content_base64. Keep document_id unchanged; this creates a new version of the same document instead of a duplicate.

Redwood stale-version recovery procedure: if upload rejects expected_version as stale, download the current version, reconcile your replacement against it, and retry with the same document_id and the new current expected_version. Never remove document_id to bypass the conflict.

Redwood replacement shortcut proposal: "Omit document_id after a version conflict and upload the bytes as a new file." This shortcut was rejected because it creates a duplicate; it is not the adopted replacement procedure.

Redwood replacement verification procedure: after an upload succeeds, download the same document_id pinned to the returned version and compare the downloaded bytes' SHA-256 with the replacement bytes' SHA-256. Matching hashes verify the stored replacement bytes. Search snippets and upload completion alone are not this byte comparison.

cases.query: How do I update an existing Redwood document without making a duplicate, verify that the stored bytes match my replacement, and recover if expected_version is stale?

required_support.quote: call upload with the existing document_id, the current expected_version, and replacement content_base64.
download the same document_id pinned to the returned version and compare the downloaded bytes' SHA-256 with the replacement bytes' SHA-256.
download the current version, reconcile your replacement against it, and retry with the same document_id and the new current expected_version.

forbidden_support.quote: Omit document_id after a version conflict and upload the bytes as a new file.

cases.rationale: All three adopted procedures are required: replace the same identity, verify exact stored bytes, and reconcile a stale-version conflict. Rejected advice to create a new identity cannot substitute for conflict recovery.
